extracted.intended_audience: members and staff of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations; Volkswagen and EPA witnesses; oversight investigators and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript and prepared statements for a House Oversight and Investigations subcommittee hearing into Volkswagen's alleged installation of defeat-device software and related EPA compliance. The document sets out informational, evidentiary, and procedural expectations for witnesses and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely production of documents and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documents and information to the committee as quickly as possible, including documents that have already been discussed publicly in connection with Volkswagen’s various Board meetings in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects voluntary, rapid disclosure of relevant records; staff authorized to make appropriate redactions before entry into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with the committee’s inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Volkswagen (and other witnesses) must cooperate with the subcommittee’s bipartisan investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation includes appearing voluntarily, answering questions, producing documents, and responding to follow-up questions submitted for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full factual disclosure about what was done and why
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the current understanding of VW executives about what exactly was done to these engines and was it done to deliberately deceive Government regulations and regulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses should provide technical descriptions of the defeat device, its operation, and the corporate rationale or intent behind its deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of responsible individuals and timeline (what did you know and when?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who was involved in the design/installation/approval of the defeat device and when responsible parties knew about the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee seeks to establish accountability across U.S. and German organization structures and to determine when executives became aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe remedial measures and compensation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what VW is doing to fix the problem and make whole those who have been affected by the actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific remediation approaches, timelines, and whether owners and dealers will be compensated or otherwise made whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and disclose impact of fixes on performance and fuel economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear information on whether any fix required of the automaker will negatively affect vehicle performance or fuel economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA and VW must analyze and communicate the effects of remedies on drivability, economy, and emissions to ensure customer expectations are managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why EPA compliance testing and audits failed to detect the issue
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must answer why standard compliance tests and audits failed to detect problems, especially in older technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include description of testing protocols, audit frequency, limitations, and any needed changes to detect similar schemes in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure remedies are effective for State inspection regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify an effective remedy so that vehicles, once fixed, will pass State emissions inspections and owners will not be subject to fines under State law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should coordinate with State requirements and explain how fixes will restore compliance for jurisdictions with periodic emissions testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify excess emissions and mitigation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how much extra pollution (tons of NOx, etc.) resulted from the defeat device and how those excess tons will be mitigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA stated it has not yet done the math; committee expects an emissions quantification and a mitigation strategy as part of the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine scope: how many vehicles and geographic distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the number of U.S. vehicles affected (noting ~482,000 cited) and where these vehicles are registered (state-by-state breakdown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data supports assessment of environmental/public health impacts and informs coordination with State agencies and attorneys general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether similar defeat devices exist in other manufacturers’ vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate whether software similar to what was used by VW is present in any other U.S. vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA’s ongoing testing should address this question; committee expects clear answers about broader industry practices or risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess sincerity/effectiveness of prior voluntary recall actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether VW’s December 2014 voluntary recall was an earnest effort to fix emissions issues or a ruse to buy time with regulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pre- and post-recall test results (e.g., CARB’s testing) and internal communications/documents to judge the recall’s adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and produce cross-jurisdictional materials (e.g., German board meeting documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documents that have been discussed publicly in connection with Volkswagen’s various Board meetings in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects full cooperation across international corporate records that illuminate decision-making and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, clear and consistent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: VW must demonstrate transparency, cooperation, and clear, consistent communication with the committee, EPA, regulators, customers, suppliers, dealers, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment to open information flow is treated as part of rebuilding public trust and facilitating remediation and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect dealers and employees from undue economic harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and address the economic impact on family-owned dealerships and employees resulting from vehicles sitting unsold and market disruptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects VW to consider implications for dealers and workforce and to propose relief or mitigation measures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with State attorneys general and environmental agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA and the committee should engage with State attorneys general and environmental directors to determine residence of affected vehicles and local impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States are expected participants; EPA has met with State environmental directors and should share relevant findings and remediation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory approval condition for new models
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA (and CARB) may withhold approval of future model-year diesel vehicles (e.g., 2016) until emissions issues are explained and resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory approval is contingent on demonstration that new-model emissions meet legal requirements and that issues are not systemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to committee questions submitted for the record within 10 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee rules provide that members have 10 days to submit additional questions for the record and expect witnesses to respond promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses should answer submitted questions in the record as part of formal post-hearing follow-up and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate corporate knowledge and communication with regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what Volkswagen told regulators over the last year as EPA and CARB tried to figure out why vehicle emissions were out of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review correspondence, meeting notes, and internal explanations provided to agencies to detect misrepresentation or concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate commitment to rebuild public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: If VW is serious about rebuilding broken trust, leaders must demonstrate a serious commitment by answering questions and taking remedial actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment is shown through transparency, corrective actions, compensation, and structural changes to prevent recurrence.
